Hey, I'm kinda new to the game development community, but I have a few monsters I've been drawing out and want to draw them in 3D. Are there any programs you would suggest to newbies? I've tried looking but I have no idea how to tell when programs actually help with 3d modeling.
Blender. Perfect starting program for 3D modeling that is absolutely free.

CGcookie.com has the best blender tutorials, or they did when I was learning. Now less of them are free and the site redesign is annoying. Their introduction to blender videos are pretty good, though. You can find it here.
I'd also recommend blender, but it's not a starter program nor is it particularly newbie friendly. Well worth learning though.
It's the best thing there is for newbies. I learned 3D modelling through it.

I'd personally consider max or maya much more user friendly for a beginner, Blender's UI is pretty opaque, but if you're starting from scratch, there's not much point building up familiarity with a system which is going to cost you thousands of dollars if you want to use it for anything.
After looking at the price tag for autodesk products. I'm kinda shying away from their stuff.

I learned to use Max in college. It has a bad rep, and there's alot of cruft, but it's actually a pretty nifty program. Then I tried to buy a copy to do freelance work and not only was it unaffordable, they insisted I buy it through authorised resellers in my region who wanted to bundle it with hundreds of euros worth of training. The software itself was €3500 or so, but with training it topped out at €5000 I think.

And to add insult to injury, the training was ridiculously basic. As in stuff a complete beginner could pick up in a few hours from a tutorial.
This is why I like Blender. They offer that shit for free.

I would also respectfully disagree, I've tried most of the other packages available, max, maya, lightwave, etc. And for me blender just clicked. Honestly I don't think it matters much what you choose, there will always be a learning curve attached. blender does what I want easily. but continuously repeating this tired old mantra that blender isnt easy for noobs is not helpful to anyone.

Glad to hear it.

I'm not trying to put anyone off blender, I use it all the time and I recommended it above, I'm just warning the OP that it's no cakewalk.

That said, I started using it back in the 2.4 days, so I might have an exaggerated opinion of what it's like for a newbie coming into it now.

If you're a student, you can get both 3D Studio Max and Maya free for educational purposes. Both are industry standard, and would be good to learn, if your plan is to eventually try to go pro. In the end, it comes down to personal preference; try a bunch of stuff, and see what clicks with you.

Addendum: You should also give 3d sculpting a look: Z-Brush, Sculptris, Mudbox, 3d Coat. All of them have either demos or educational versions. Sculptris is free.
Are you a student in a university? If so you can get free autodesk software.

Blender is free and open source, so it's a no risk place to get started. It isn't necessarily intuitive, but if you follow some tutorials you can get started pretty easily. There is a good community for it over at http://blenderartists.org/forum/

Good luck.

What's the trick?

Is it simply posting based on a behavioral pattern (eg: here's Sparky my dog with one last meal before we put him sleep tends to hit the front page often) or is there a whole multi-step process involved?

Thanks for asking this. I was hoping someone would ask for more specifics.

There are a lot of tricks. The most important of which is to have something people care about. In your Sparky example, that alone might be enough to get traction if posted at the right time. If you were to throw in your other dog looking sad or a family member crying in the background, it would increase the feels the image gets, which should engage the user to the viral level.

The more layers the better because you can't know what each person is attracted to the most.

Timing is probably the most underrated thing about any post. I can get things way more visible by just timing the post. I know that it generally takes around 6 hours from the post to start reaching the frontpage. The next morning after that is when all the big blogs and news sources will pick it up. That's when it can go super viral. If you can make this whole process before super viral last 48 hours, you will milk the exposure for as much as it's worth.
